$comment: Locked meanings for PDL built-in objects. Authors and hosts treat this file as the vocabulary. Compilers still type-check from shared/frame-props.json (enum case lists must match). Host-protocol channel/verb names must match test-fixtures/pdl/stdlib/host_protocols.pdl. Declaration names must match shared/keywords.json (declarations group). Edit meanings here; run npm run docs:gen.

sectionIntros.declarations: The top-level blocks in a `.pdl` file. Use them to import files, name tokens, and define components. Order inside a file is free.
sectionIntros.frames: Every component has one root frame. Nested UI is the same four constructors on `let`. Use `layout` to group, `text` for words, `icon` for a glyph, `media` for an image or video. Unknown properties are PDL-E011; wrong types are PDL-E006.
sectionIntros.children: `children` belongs on `Layout` — that is how PDL draws views and nested views. A child `Layout` has its own `children`. `Text()`, `Icon()`, and `Media()` are leaves: they do not take `children` and do not nest views. Every entry is a component — a built-in frame or one you declared (`Button(…)`). Name them with `let`, then mount them with `children = [heading, save]`. A `let` that never appears in `children` is not drawn. A `let` mounts at most once (PDL-E042); two identical-looking children are two lets or a list. `Spacer()` is the leftover-space exception. A `ForEach` block does not mount views by itself.
sectionIntros.spacer: A child that eats leftover space on the main axis. Write `Spacer()` inside `children = […]`.
sectionIntros.forEach: Use ForEach when a list needs per-row state or click handling — which chip is selected, which row is highlighted. It writes onto items you already put in `children`. It does not create views by itself.
sectionIntros.repeat: `Repeat(count:, begin: = 1) { i in … }` mounts N copies at bake. Index domain is `begin` … `begin + count − 1` (default begin 1). Nested Repeat is allowed; each count ≤ 32 and nested product ≤ 64. Equality on binders (`i == currentPage`) is OK — not Number algebra. Distinct from ForEach.
sectionIntros.let: Name a nested frame, or a typed value you reuse in props. Prefer a lowercase id (`let title`, `let ramp`) so the name is not the same word as the type. Frame lets go in `children`. Typed value lets do not.
sectionIntros.parameters: The public inbound API of a component. Every name in the parentheses is public. There is no private parameter.
sectionIntros.variants: Closed sets you declare — tone, size, filter id. Write `.case` at use sites. `enum` and `variant` are the same in v1.
sectionIntros.self: The enclosing component instance. Use `self.param` when a nested name would shadow. Rules-query `self` is a different thing.
sectionIntros.conditionals: Change a handful of properties when a parameter or state changes. First match wins.
sectionIntros.conditions: Comparisons and booleans used in `if` and ForEach. Keep `&&` and `||` in separate expressions, or parenthesize.
sectionIntros.null: Clear a frame or typeStyle property so the default applies. Not a token value.
sectionIntros.tokenTypes: Named values you declare once and reuse. Write `primitive` for the raw palette and `semantic` for the names components should use (`color.surface`). Pick a type when a property needs a color, a gap, a shadow, and so on. Duration, Ease, Timing, Pose, Stagger, Motion, and PresentationMotion are the motion types — they exist for handler `animate =`, frame `animate`, and Presenter pair clips. Effect is paint: `.blurSelf` softens the node, `.blurBehind` samples what is behind.
sectionIntros.theme: A named remap of tokens you already declared. Use a theme for light/dark, brand, or reduced motion. Components keep using semantic names; the theme changes what those names resolve to.
sectionIntros.catalog: A named remap the environment applies — platform icon sets, not light/dark. Same override lines as a theme. Only `use catalog Name` inside `mount` applies it. The theme picker must not list catalogs.
sectionIntros.host: An environment profile: `host Name(params) [mount { … }]`. Components opt in with `<Host>` to read those params. Width-class and surface taxonomies are pack-local variants, not language types. Bake runs `mount` once against an opaque facts bag, then any fact whose key matches a host param pins that param for every `<Host>` component.
sectionIntros.typeStyle: A named bundle of text-frame properties. A text frame sets `style = Name`. Body lines are the same properties as a text frame.
sectionIntros.values: Structured values you pass to properties — insets, shadows, corners, gradient stops.
sectionIntros.layers: Fills stacked in `background` and `foreground`. A hex Color is usually enough; use these constructors for a gradient or a `MediaLayer`. `Blur()` in a fill list is the alias window for a behind pane — prefer `effect = Effect(.blurBehind, …)` on the frame.
sectionIntros.assets: How you point at a glyph or a file. `IconRef` is the Icon token RHS; `MediaSource` is the source for a `media` frame and `MediaLayer`.
sectionIntros.enums: Closed choices such as `.row` or `.center`. Use them on layout properties and as parameter types.
sectionIntros.eventDirections: A component hears its parameters. That is enough for a fixture, and for a parent that already knows the state. It is not enough when the user clicks a chip, or when a field should start editing. PDL does not run like a script in the page. The host — the preview, or the app that embeds the design — delivers pointer and text events onto a component that opted in (`<PointerInput>`, `<EditableText>`). The component can then emit a typed channel to its parent (`select`, `change`). The parent assigns on that channel and its own parameters update, so the row can show which chip is selected. A component can also ask the host to do something, such as begin editing. Those are three different paths. A `pressEnd` is not an emit.
sectionIntros.emits:
How a child tells its parent something happened — a chip was selected, a field changed. Declare the channel with `emits { … }` or inherit it with `emits

`, fire it from a click, and listen on the parent. `emits

` is also how a component fills a `[P]` slot.
sectionIntros.protocols:
A shared contract so several components can sit in the same list and speak the same language. `<>` receives: host inbound (`PointerInput`) and ancestor sinks (`ShowEpisode` on the screen). `emits

` sends: fire that protocol’s channels, inherit its params, and satisfy `[P]` slots.
sectionIntros.hostPrelude: A host protocol lets the preview (or app) trigger component changes: hover color, a click, focus, typing — or, with `Host`, read the active environment profile. Use `PointerInput` for buttons and chips; use `EditableText` for a field the user types into; use `Host` on a structural parent. Opt in with `component C <PointerInput>`. List more than one when needed: `component C <Host, PointerInput>`. These names are built in — you do not import them.
sectionIntros.motion: One `animate =` assignment on a host handler, or a standing `animate` on any frame. Its type is Motion: a Transition, an optional play mode, Pose or keys, Stagger, and finite repeat. A bare Transition is sugar for Motion(transition: …). Bake stays at rest; the HTML host plays a CSS overlay.
sectionIntros.samples: Reusable catalogs of instances you mount in layout so a prototype can stay interactive — a library of tracks, a set of chips, an empty list you can switch to. Write the catalog once and point at `Tracks.library.tracks` from a parameter default or from `children`. Isolated component examples, the kind you would put in design-system documentation, belong in fixtures.
sectionIntros.fixtures: A fixture is a named bag of parameter values for one component, plus optional bake knobs (`host`, `theme`, `hostFacts`). The Playground Fixture menu shows the labels. Each `example` is concrete values only — not other parameters, not layout. Flip through them to preview states without editing the component. Use fixtures for the examples you would put in design-system documentation — primary vs secondary, large vs small. Use them also for a whole view: empty search, a night playlist, mid-rename. Samples are the catalogs you mount; a fixture chooses which world the preview is in.
sectionIntros.usage: A written note on a component for authors and tools. In v1 the only key is `description`.
sectionIntros.extend: Add fixtures, usage, or rules to a component you imported — without copying its layout.
sectionIntros.rule: A design check the preview or CI can flag. It does not change how anything looks. Tag instances in a `rules` block, then write a query from this instance — siblings, children, parent — and a strength (`.must` fails the build; `.should` warns).

frameKinds.name: layout
frameKinds.meaning: A flex-like container — the usual root of a component, and any nested group. Write `component Card layout { … }` for the root, or `let box = Layout(…)` for a nested group. Set `direction` to `.row` or `.column` (or `.stack` to overlap). Named children go in `children`. Spacing is `gap` / `padding` (Distance and EdgeInsets). Alignment is `align` and `justify`.

frameKinds.name: text
frameKinds.meaning: A typography node. `content` is the string. Prefer `style:` naming a typeStyle for size and weight; override with `color`, `fontSize`, and the other text properties when needed. Root form is `component Title text { … }`; nested form is `let heading = Text(…)`.
frameKinds.example: let heading = Text(content: title, style: Title, color: color.text)

frameKinds.name: icon
frameKinds.meaning: A small tintable glyph. The `icon` property is an Icon token or `IconRef` — not this frame. Set `size` or `width` / `height`. Tint with `color`. Nested form is `let star = Icon(…)`.
frameKinds.example: let star = Icon(icon: IconRef(system: .sfSymbols, name: "star"), size: 16, color: color.ink)

frameKinds.name: media
frameKinds.meaning: A box that draws raster, vector, or video from a MediaSource. Distinct from MediaLayer, which is a fill inside `background` / `foreground`. Fit the source with `contentMode` (`.cover`, `.contain`, …). Nested form is `let photo = Media(…)`.
frameKinds.example: let photo = Media(source: media.hero, contentMode: .cover, height: 120)

paramScalars.name: String
paramScalars.meaning: Quoted text. Component parameters, text content, font family, easing strings.

paramScalars.name: Number
paramScalars.meaning: A finite number. Unitless unless the property says otherwise (Duration is milliseconds; Opacity is 0…1; LineHeight is a ratio). Params may add coherence bounds: `Number(min: 2, max: 10)`. Named aliases: `type PageCount = Number(min: 2, max: 10)`. Bake / fixtures keep a scalar; out-of-range is PDL-E057.

tokenTypes.name: Color
tokenTypes.meaning: A fill, text, or border color. Hex is a color, not a string.

accept.meaning: Three-digit hex.
Six-digit hex. The usual literal.
Eight-digit hex; last pair is alpha.
A Color token (semantic on components).
Tint: multiply alpha. Prefer an Opacity token on the right.
Tint with a named Opacity.

reject.meaning: Quoted hex is PDL-E017.

tokenTypes.example:
primitive color.primitive.blue.500: Color = #3B82F6
semantic color.surface: Color = color.primitive.blue.500
background = color.surface @ opacity.surface.tint

tokenTypes.name: Opacity
tokenTypes.meaning: An alpha multiplier in 0…1. Name it so themes can remap scrims and tints. A bare Opacity token is not a layer — apply it with `color @ opacity` or an `opacity:` argument.

accept.meaning: Number in 0…1. Fine for a primitive; avoid raw decimals on library surfaces.
An Opacity token. Preferred on the right of `@` and on `opacity=`.

tokenTypes.example:
primitive opacity.primitive.scrim: Opacity = 0.4
semantic opacity.surface.tint: Opacity = opacity.primitive.scrim
foreground = color.ink @ opacity.surface.tint

tokenTypes.name: Distance
tokenTypes.meaning: A non-negative length in design units (pixels in the HTML preview). Used for gaps and inset axes. Not a string; there is no `px` suffix.

accept.meaning: Non-negative number.
A Distance token (semantic alias of a primitive).

reject.meaning: No unit suffix.
Negative lengths are rejected.

tokenTypes.example:
primitive spacing.primitive.md: Distance = 12
semantic space.stack: Distance = spacing.primitive.md
gap = space.stack

tokenTypes.name: Radius
tokenTypes.meaning: A uniform corner radius (or a blur radius amount). A number. Per-corner values are CornerRadii via `Corner(…)`, which is not a Radius token RHS.

accept.meaning: Non-negative number.
A Radius token.

reject.meaning: That produces CornerRadii, not Radius. PDL-E005 on a Radius token.

tokenTypes.example:
primitive radius.primitive.md: Radius = 10
semantic radius.card: Radius = radius.primitive.md
cornerRadius = radius.card

tokenTypes.name: Shadow
tokenTypes.meaning: A drop shadow. Axes are numbers (or numeric tokens); color is a Color. Optional spread defaults to 0. HTML preview maps the resolved object to CSS box-shadow.

accept.meaning: Required fields. color may be hex, a Color token, or `color @ opacity`.
Optional spread; omit for 0.
A Shadow token.

reject.meaning: A CSS box-shadow string is PDL-E005.

tokenTypes.example:
primitive shadow.card: Shadow = Shadow(x: 0, y: 4, blurRadius: 12, color: #000000 @ 0.15)
shadow = shadow.card

tokenTypes.name: Icon
tokenTypes.meaning: A tintable glyph reference. This is the value of an icon frame’s `icon:` property — not the Icon() frame constructor.

accept.meaning: SF Symbol. System is IconSystem.
Material Symbol.
Pack-relative file. No leading /.
Path sugar: must contain `/` and/or a known extension.
An Icon token.

reject.meaning: Bare glyph id is ambiguous — PDL-E005.
That builds an icon frame, not an Icon token.

tokenTypes.example:
primitive icon.primitive.star: Icon = IconRef(system: .sfSymbols, name: "star")
semantic icon.action.favorite: Icon = icon.primitive.star
icon = icon.action.favorite

tokenTypes.name: MediaSource
tokenTypes.meaning: Where a raster, vector, or video comes from. Distinct from the Media() frame and from MediaLayer (a fill).

accept.meaning: Pack-relative file. No leading /. Kind/format inferred from a known extension when omitted.
Remote http(s) URL.
Opaque CDN address: set kind (and format when known). Kind and format must agree (PDL-E006).
Path-string sugar.
URL-string sugar.
A MediaSource token.

tokenTypes.example:
primitive media.hero: MediaSource = MediaSource(url: "https://cdn.example/abc", kind: .raster, format: .jpeg)
source = media.hero

tokenTypes.name: Ratio
tokenTypes.meaning: A positive width/height ratio.

accept.meaning: Positive number (width ÷ height).
W:H sugar; same as 16/9.
A Ratio token.

tokenTypes.example:
primitive ratio.video: Ratio = 16:9
width = .aspect(ratio.video)

tokenTypes.name: FontFamily
tokenTypes.meaning: A font stack. Quoted string.

accept.meaning: CSS-style stack.
A FontFamily token.

tokenTypes.example:
primitive font.body: FontFamily = "Inter, system-ui, sans-serif"
fontFamily = font.body

tokenTypes.name: Size
tokenTypes.meaning: Font size or icon box size in design units. Unitless — not `16px`.

accept.meaning: Number.
A Size token.

tokenTypes.example:
primitive type.size.body: Size = 16
fontSize = type.size.body

tokenTypes.name: Weight
tokenTypes.meaning: Font weight as a number (400, 500, 600, …).

accept.meaning: Numeric weight.
A Weight token.

tokenTypes.example:
primitive type.weight.medium: Weight = 500
fontWeight = type.weight.medium

tokenTypes.name: LineHeight
tokenTypes.meaning: Leading as a unitless ratio of fontSize. 1.35 means 135%. Must be greater than 0.

accept.meaning: Positive number.
A LineHeight token.

tokenTypes.example:
primitive type.lineHeight.body: LineHeight = 1.35
lineHeight = type.lineHeight.body

tokenTypes.name: LetterSpacing
tokenTypes.meaning: Tracking in em — a fraction of fontSize. May be negative.

accept.meaning: Number in em.
A LetterSpacing token.

tokenTypes.example:
primitive type.letterSpacing.tight: LetterSpacing = -0.01
letterSpacing = type.letterSpacing.tight

tokenTypes.name: Sizing
tokenTypes.meaning: How a width or height is computed. Write `.hug` or `Sizing.hug`. A bare number on a sizing property means `.fixed(n)`. Rare as a token; usual on frames.

accept.meaning: Size to content.
Fill the parent on that axis.
Exactly n design units.
On width/height, the same as `.fixed(240)`.
Flexible range. Any field may be omitted. All omitted is like .fill. preferred maps to flex-basis (or the host equivalent).
Derive this axis from the other so width/height = r. r is a number, W:H, or a Ratio token. Put .aspect on the free axis only.
A Sizing token.

tokenTypes.example:
primitive sizing.sidebar: Sizing = .fill
width = .fill
height = .hug
width = 240

tokenTypes.name: Duration
tokenTypes.meaning: Animation length in milliseconds. Unitless — not `150ms`.

accept.meaning: Milliseconds.
A Duration token.

tokenTypes.example:
primitive motion.duration.fast: Duration = 150
primitive motion.duration.standard: Duration = 250

tokenTypes.name: Ease
tokenTypes.meaning: How time is shaped. Named cases `.linear` / `.in` / `.out`, or `Ease.bezier(x1, y1, x2, y2)`. x1 and x2 must be 0…1 (CSS time axis). y1 and y2 may overshoot. Not a CSS string.

accept.meaning: Decelerate into rest.
Cubic bezier. x1/x2 in 0…1; y may overshoot.
An Ease token.

tokenTypes.example:
primitive motion.ease.standard: Ease = Ease.bezier(0.2, 0, 0, 1)
primitive motion.ease.linear: Ease = .linear

tokenTypes.name: Timing
tokenTypes.meaning: A duration plus ease, and an optional delay (default 0). Written `Timing(duration:, ease: [, delay:])`. Themes replace a Timing wholly — no deep merge. A Timing is valid `animate =` sugar for `Motion(timing: …)`.

accept.meaning: Required fields. Values may be literals or Duration / Ease tokens.
Optional delay in milliseconds.
A Timing token.

tokenTypes.example:
semantic motion.appear: Timing = Timing(duration: motion.duration.standard, ease: motion.ease.standard)
semantic motion.instant: Timing = Timing(duration: 0, ease: .linear)

tokenTypes.name: Pose
tokenTypes.meaning: An overlay snapshot — not layout. Used on appear / dismiss, hover flourish, keys, and standing frame `animate`. Fields: opacity (0…1), scale (unitless), scaleX, scaleY, translateX, translateY, blur (CSS px), rotate (degrees), originX / originY (0…1, transform origin). At least one field is required. Unknown labels are PDL-E005. Appear plays from the pose to rest; dismiss plays from rest to the pose; other sites follow `play`. Themes replace a Pose wholly — no field merge.

accept.meaning: Constructor. All fields optional except that one must be present.
A Pose token.

tokenTypes.example: semantic pose.fadeUp: Pose = Pose(opacity: 0, scale: 0.95, translateY: 8)

tokenTypes.name: Stagger
tokenTypes.meaning: How a pose track is distributed across the handler’s direct visible children. `step` is a Duration (milliseconds). `from` is `.first` or `.last` (default `.first`). Illegal without `pose:` or `keys:` on the same Motion. Themes replace a Stagger wholly.

accept.meaning: Step only; direction defaults to `.first`.
Or `from: .last`.
A Stagger token.

tokenTypes.example: semantic motion.stagger.list: Stagger = Stagger(step: 30, from: .first)

tokenTypes.name: Motion
tokenTypes.meaning: The value of `animate =` (handler or frame). Joins a clock with an optional Play, Pose or keys, Stagger, and finite repeat. Declare `duration:` / `ease:` / optional `delay:` on the Motion, or pass `timing:` as a Timing token or `Timing(…)`. Do not mix `timing:` with flattened clock fields (E005). `pose:` and `keys:` together are rejected. `play: .loop` is forever — do not also set `repeat:`. `stagger` and `repeat` require a pose track. Omit `play` on reusable tokens so the site default applies. A Timing token or `Timing(…)` is sugar for `Motion(timing: …)`. Themes replace a Motion wholly — no field merge.

accept.meaning: Curve only — hover / implicit interpolation.
Lifecycle overlay. Handler name is the direction.

accept.form: Motion(duration: 250, ease: .out, pose: pose.fadeUp, stagger: Stagger(step: 30, from: .first))
accept.meaning: Full join with an explicit clock.
Shallow copy of a Motion token; labeled fields replace those fields.
A Timing token — sugar for Motion(timing: that).
A Timing constructor — same sugar.
A Motion token.

tokenTypes.example:
semantic motion.hoverPop: Motion = Motion(timing: motion.appear, keys: [Key(pose: Pose(scale: 1.12), at: 1)])
hoverEnd = { animate = Motion(motion.hoverPop, play: .toRest) }

tokenTypes.name: PresentationMotion
tokenTypes.meaning: A Presenter pair clip. `incoming` plays `.toRest` (mounts at pose, eases to rest). `outgoing` plays `.toPose`. Pair-level `duration` / `ease` / `delay` apply when a slot is a Pose. A Motion slot keeps its own clock. A Motion with `keys:` plays that path as authored (`Key.ease` is the curve to the next stop). `front` is who starts on top (`.incoming` or `.outgoing`). Omit it: `move` keeps incoming on top; `dismissMove` keeps outgoing on top. `switchAt` is a Duration in milliseconds — wall-clock from play start, not eased progress. Omit it to keep `front` the whole clip. `.reversed` swaps sides and time-reverses `ease` (`.in`↔`.out`; bezier control points invert). `delay` stays. Omit `switchAt`: flip `front`. With `switchAt`: keep `front` (the side swap remaps who that label is) and invert to `span − switchAt` (span is max of each side’s delay + duration). `keys:` paths are not reversed — write `dismissMove:` for that.

accept.form: PresentationMotion(incoming: Pose(translateX: 390), outgoing: Pose(translateX: -48, opacity: 0.86), duration: 320, ease: .out)
accept.meaning: Push-style pair. Omit front: move keeps incoming on top.
Who starts on top. `.incoming` or `.outgoing`.
Switch who is on top at that many milliseconds from play start.

accept.form: PresentationMotion(incoming: Pose(scale: 0.92, translateX: -36), outgoing: Pose(scale: 0.92, translateX: 36), duration: 480, ease: .in, front: .outgoing, switchAt: 240)
accept.meaning: Card swap: outgoing starts in front; incoming takes front at 240ms.
Swap incoming/outgoing, time-reverse ease. No switchAt: flip front. With switchAt: keep front, invert to span − switchAt. Key lists stay.

accept.form: incoming: Motion(duration: 480, ease: .out, keys: [Key(pose: Pose(translateX: 390), at: 0), Key(pose: .rest, at: 1)])
accept.meaning: Keyed incoming path. Played as authored. Per-key `ease:` is the curve to the next stop.

tokenTypes.example:
semantic motion.navPush: PresentationMotion = PresentationMotion(
  incoming: Pose(translateX: 390),
  outgoing: Pose(translateX: -48, opacity: 0.86),
  duration: 320,
  ease: .out
)
semantic motion.cardSwap: PresentationMotion = PresentationMotion(
  incoming: Pose(scale: 0.92, translateX: -36),
  outgoing: Pose(scale: 0.92, translateX: 36),
  duration: 480,
  ease: .in,
  front: .outgoing,
  switchAt: 240
)

tokenTypes.name: Effect
tokenTypes.meaning: A paint-time distortion on a frame — not a fill, not a child. `.blurSelf` softens this node's pixels (`filter`). `.blurBehind` samples what is behind (`backdrop-filter`). `.glass` is reserved. `blur = n` is sugar for `Effect(.blurSelf, radius: n)`. One `effect` per frame. `Blur()` in a fill list is the alias window for `.blurBehind`.

accept.meaning: Soften this node's pixels.
Pane over what is behind. Optional vibrancy:.
An Effect token.
Only on `blur =` — sugar for Effect(.blurSelf, radius: 8).

reject.meaning: Effect is not a layer. Set effect = on the frame.
Not a frame. Wear the effect on a child layout.
Reserved — not implemented yet.

tokenTypes.example:
primitive effect.frost: Effect = Effect(.blurBehind, radius: 20)
sheet.effect = effect.frost
photo.blur = 8

tokenTypes.name: Blur
tokenTypes.meaning: A blur layer object (alias window). Prefer `effect = Effect(.blurBehind, radius:)` on the frame. Radius amounts reuse Radius — there is no numeric Blur token. A bare Blur token is still a valid layer entry. Legacy `Blur(blur: …)` is rejected.

accept.meaning: Radius is a number or Radius token.
Optional BlurStyle. v1 ships only .standard.
Optional Vibrancy.
A Blur token; legal inside a layer list.

reject.meaning: A bare number is a Radius, not a Blur.
Legacy argument name — rejected.

tokenTypes.example:
primitive blur.sheet.radius: Radius = 16
primitive blur.sheet: Blur = Blur(radius: blur.sheet.radius)
background = [blur.sheet, color.surface]

tokenTypes.name: Vibrancy
tokenTypes.meaning: Saturation and brightness for a blur (or as its own layer token).

accept.meaning: Both fields are numbers.
A Vibrancy token; legal as a layer entry.

tokenTypes.example:
primitive vibrancy.sheet: Vibrancy = Vibrancy(saturation: 1.2, brightness: 1.05)
primitive blur.sheet: Blur = Blur(radius: 16, vibrancy: vibrancy.sheet)

tokenTypes.name: Ramp
tokenTypes.meaning: An opacity or color ramp along an axis. Direction is RampDirection. Stops are GradientStop values.

accept.meaning: Preferred constructor.
Naked tuple; still accepted.
A Ramp token.

tokenTypes.example:
primitive ramp.fade.bottom: Ramp = Ramp(
  direction: .bottomToTop,
  stops: [
    GradientStop(opacity: 1, position: 0.5),
    GradientStop(opacity: 0, position: 1)
  ]
)

tokenTypes.name: EdgeInsets
tokenTypes.meaning: A box inset. Axes may be numbers or Distance tokens. A bare number on padding, margin, or inset means uniform insets on all four sides. That sugar does not apply to gap.

accept.meaning: Horizontal and vertical pairs.
Per-side.
On padding / margin / inset only: uniform EdgeInsets.
An EdgeInsets token.

tokenTypes.example:
primitive spacing.card.pad: EdgeInsets = EdgeInsets(x: 16, y: 12)
padding = spacing.card.pad
padding = 16
margin = EdgeInsets(top: 8, right: 12, bottom: 8, left: 12)

tokenTypes.name: CornerRadii
tokenTypes.meaning: Per-corner radii. The type name is CornerRadii; the constructor name is Corner. Axes are numbers or Radius tokens. A Radius token stays uniform — do not assign Corner(…) to a Radius token.

accept.meaning: Asymmetric radii on a frame’s cornerRadius.
On cornerRadius, a number is a uniform Radius, not CornerRadii.

tokenTypes.name: Media
tokenTypes.meaning: A media fill inside a background or foreground stack. Construct with MediaLayer. Not the Media() frame, and not a MediaSource (that is the address).

accept.meaning: source is a MediaSource; contentMode is ContentMode. Optional opacity:.
A Media (layer) token or value-let.

reject.meaning: That builds a media frame, not a layer fill.
Do not postfix @ if opacity: is already set (PDL-E020).

tokenTypes.example:
let hero: Media = MediaLayer(source: media.hero, contentMode: .cover)
background = [hero, color.surface]

tokenTypes.name: GradientStop
tokenTypes.meaning: One stop in a Ramp. Position is 0…1. Supply opacity, color, or both.

accept.meaning: Fade stop.
Color stop.
Both.

tokenTypes.example:
let fadeOut: GradientStop = GradientStop(opacity: 0, position: 1)
stops = [GradientStop(opacity: 1, position: 0), fadeOut]

tokenTypes.name: Background
tokenTypes.meaning: A named layer stack composited under children. Same right-hand side as Foreground: a color, or an ordered list of layers. Prefer `color @ opacityToken` over raw decimals. A bare Opacity token is not a layer.

accept.meaning: Scalar color sugar — one solid layer.
Ordered layers, bottom first.
A Background token.

tokenTypes.example:
semantic material.sheet: Background = [blur.sheet, color.surface @ opacity.surface.tint]
background = material.sheet

tokenTypes.name: Foreground
tokenTypes.meaning: A named layer stack composited over children. Same right-hand side as Background.

accept.meaning: Scalar color sugar.
Layer list.
A Foreground token.

tokenTypes.example:
semantic fg.hoverTint: Foreground = [color.ink @ opacity.state.hover]
foreground = fg.hoverTint

enums.name: Direction
enums.meaning: Main axis of a layout (or overlap mode for stack).

cases.meaning: Main axis left to right.
Main axis top to bottom.
Main axis right to left.
Main axis bottom to top.
Children share one box. Array order is painter’s order: first at the back, last on top.
Same overlap as stack; first child is on top.

enums.name: Wrap
enums.meaning: Whether children wrap to another line on the main axis.

cases.meaning: Keep children on one line (default).
Wrap onto additional lines. rowGap / columnGap apply.

enums.name: Align
enums.meaning: Cross-axis alignment in a layout; vertical placement of text or media content in its box.

cases.meaning: Toward the start of the cross axis (top in a row; left in a column). On text/media: top of the box.
Centered on the cross axis (or vertically in a text/media box).
Toward the end of the cross axis. On text/media: bottom of the box.
Stretch on the cross axis. Layout only — illegal on text and media (PDL-E006).

enums.name: Justify
enums.meaning: Main-axis distribution in a layout; horizontal placement of text or media content in its box.

cases.meaning: Pack toward the start of the main axis. On text/media: left of the box.
Centered on the main axis (or horizontally in a text/media box).
Pack toward the end. On text/media: right of the box.
Stretch along the main axis. Layout only — illegal on text and media (PDL-E006).
First and last flush to the ends; even space between. Layout only.
Even space around each child. Layout only.

enums.name: Overflow
enums.meaning: What happens when content does not fit the frame. There is no .hidden or .auto.

cases.meaning: Content may paint outside the box.
Content clips and the host may scroll.
Content is clipped; no scroll. Use this instead of CSS overflow:hidden.

enums.name: BorderPosition
enums.meaning: Where the stroke is painted. Borders never change the layout box size.

cases.meaning: Stroke outside the border box (default when omitted).
Stroke inside the border box.

enums.name: TruncateStyle
enums.meaning: How leftover text is cut when lineClamp is set.

cases.meaning: Hard cut after N lines; no ellipsis.
Trailing … after the last painted line. Default if lineClamp is set and truncateStyle is omitted.

enums.example: let blurb = Text(content: longCopy, lineClamp: 2, truncateStyle: .ellipsis)

enums.name: ContentMode
enums.meaning: How a media source fits its box.

cases.meaning: Fill the box; crop overflow. Preserves aspect ratio.
Fit entirely inside the box; may letterbox.
Stretch to the box; may distort.
Like contain, but never scale up above intrinsic size.

enums.example: let hero = Media(source: media.hero, contentMode: .cover, width: .fill, height: 160)

enums.name: AlignSelf
enums.meaning: Override the parent’s align for this child only.

cases.meaning: Cross-axis start, ignoring parent align.
Cross-axis center.
Cross-axis end.
Stretch on the cross axis.
Use the parent’s align (default).

enums.example:
direction = .row
align = .start
let sidebar = Layout(width: 200, alignSelf: .stretch, children: [])
children = [sidebar, body]

enums.name: Position
enums.meaning: Whether a child of a layout sits in the flex flow. Set `position` and `inset` on the **child** (constructor args or `Child.position = …`), not on the parent. There is no `x` / `y` / `top =` property. Placement is only `position` + `inset`. `inset` is EdgeInsets from the parent’s **padding box**. The child must still appear in `children` — `.absolute` does not mount it.

cases.meaning: In-flow flex child (default). `inset` is ignored.
Out of flow. Pin with `inset`. `inset = 8` is 8 on all four sides; `EdgeInsets(top:, right:, bottom:, left:)` parks a corner (use 0 on the sides you do not pin).

enums.name: BlurStyle
enums.meaning: Which blur the preview uses. v1 only has `.standard`.

cases.meaning: Default host blur. The only v1 case.

enums.name: EffectKind
enums.meaning: What an Effect samples. `.blurSelf` is this node's pixels. `.blurBehind` and `.glass` share the behind slot.

cases.meaning: Soften this frame's own pixels. CSS `filter: blur()`.
Sample what is behind this frame. CSS `backdrop-filter`.
Behind plus lighting / refraction. Reserved — not implemented yet.

enums.example:
photo.effect = Effect(.blurSelf, radius: 8)
sheet.effect = Effect(.blurBehind, radius: 16)

enums.name: Play
enums.meaning: How a Motion runs its pose track. Not a token type — only the `play:` field on Motion. Omit it on reusable tokens so the site default applies.

cases.meaning: Run the path and finish on rest (identity overlay). Default for appear, hoverEnd, and pressEnd.
Run the path and finish on the last key. Default for dismiss, hoverStart, and pressStart when a pose track is present.
Repeat the path forever. Do not also set `repeat:`.

enums.example:
hoverEnd = { animate = Motion(motion.hoverPop, play: .toRest) }
icon.animate = Motion(transition: motion.appear, play: .loop, pose: Pose(rotate: 360))

enums.name: Front
enums.meaning: Which side of a Presenter pair clip starts on top. Not a token type — only the `front:` field on PresentationMotion. Pair with `switchAt` to switch who is on top mid-clip (card swap, crossfade). Do not put crossing z on Pose.

cases.meaning: The entering page starts in front. Default for `move` when `front` is omitted.
The leaving page starts in front. Default for `dismissMove` when `front` is omitted.

enums.example:
semantic motion.cardSwap: PresentationMotion = PresentationMotion(
  incoming: Pose(scale: 0.92, translateX: -36),
  outgoing: Pose(scale: 0.92, translateX: 36),
  duration: 480,
  ease: .in,
  front: .outgoing,
  switchAt: 240
)

enums.name: RampDirection
enums.meaning: Axis of a Ramp (gradient / opacity mask). Not a frame-prop enum — only on Ramp.

cases.meaning: Linear; start at the top edge.
Linear; start at the bottom edge.
Linear; start at the left edge.
Linear; start at the right edge.
From the center. GradientStop.position is a fraction of radius (0 = center, 1 = edge).

enums.example:
background = Ramp(
  direction: .bottomToTop,
  stops: [
    GradientStop(opacity: 1, position: 0),
    GradientStop(opacity: 0, position: 1)
  ]
)

enums.name: IconSystem
enums.meaning: Which symbol library an IconRef names.

cases.meaning: SF Symbols (Apple).
Material Symbols.

enums.name: MediaKind
enums.meaning: Role of a media address when the extension is missing or ambiguous.

cases.meaning: Bitmap (JPEG, PNG, WebP, GIF, …).
SVG / PDF / design vector.
Video file or stream.

enums.name: MediaFormat
enums.meaning: Closed file format. Must agree with kind when both are set (PDL-E006). .jpg is an alias of .jpeg.

cases.meaning: WebP image.
JPEG image (.jpg is the same case).
PNG image.
GIF image.
SVG vector.
MP4 video.
WebM video.
PDF page / vector.

enums.example: primitive media.hero: MediaSource = MediaSource(url: "https://cdn.example/abc", kind: .raster, format: .jpeg)

enums.name: RuleStrength
enums.meaning: How seriously a failed Rule is treated — stop the build, or just warn.

cases.meaning: Violation is an error (fails validation / CI).
If the query matches, error.
Violation is a warning.
If the query matches, warning.

constructors.name: Layout
constructors.meaning: Build a layout frame. Arguments are the same properties as a layout body (direction:, gap:, children:, …).

constructors.name: Text
constructors.meaning: Build a text frame (content:, style:, color:, fontSize:, …).

constructors.name: Icon
constructors.meaning: Build an icon frame. The glyph is icon: (Icon token or IconRef). This is not IconRef.

constructors.name: Media
constructors.meaning: Build a media frame (source:, contentMode:, …). This is not MediaLayer.

constructors.name: Presenter
constructors.meaning: A navigation hole with a stack and an optional layered cover. `let presenter = Presenter(root: home)` then `children = [presenter, tabBar]`. The hole is a one-child layout box: `width` / `height` default to `.fill` so it occupies remaining space next to chrome; set `.hug` or a fixed size to opt out. `padding`, `align`, and `justify` inset or place a hugging page inside the hole. Bake always paints the stack top; when a cover is up it is centered over that page so the prior screen stays visible around it. `presenter.push` / `pop` / `replace` / `present(…, style: .cover)` / `dismiss` are legal only in an ancestor-capture body. Pin a stack with `presenter = [Home(), Episode()]` and a cover with `presenter.cover = Settings()`. Not a page.

constructors.name: Spacer
constructors.meaning: Zero-argument child that absorbs remaining free space on the parent’s main axis. Only legal inside `children = […]`. Write `Spacer()` — bare `Spacer` is a name. `Spacer() @ opacity` is illegal.

constructors.name: EdgeInsets
constructors.meaning: Box inset. EdgeInsets(x:, y:) or EdgeInsets(top:, right:, bottom:, left:). A number on padding/margin/inset means uniform EdgeInsets.

constructors.name: Corner
constructors.meaning: Asymmetric radii: Corner(tl:, tr:, br:, bl:). Produces CornerRadii. A number on cornerRadius is a uniform Radius.

constructors.name: Shadow
constructors.meaning: Shadow(x:, y:, blurRadius:, color: [, spread:]). Axes are numbers or numeric tokens; color is a Color. spread defaults to 0.

constructors.name: Color
constructors.meaning: Layer constructor Color(color: …). The token type Color is the same name — a hex or token is usually enough; use Color(…) inside a layer list when you need the explicit form.

constructors.name: Ramp
constructors.meaning: Ramp(direction: RampDirection, stops: [GradientStop, …]). Also a token type.

constructors.name: GradientStop
constructors.meaning: GradientStop(position: 0…1 [, opacity:] [, color:]).

constructors.name: Blur
constructors.meaning: Blur(radius: [, style: BlurStyle] [, vibrancy: Vibrancy]). Not a bare number. Legacy Blur(blur: …) is rejected.

constructors.name: Vibrancy
constructors.meaning: Vibrancy(saturation:, brightness:). Used on Blur or as its own layer token.

constructors.name: Pose
constructors.meaning: Overlay snapshot: Pose(opacity:, scale:, scaleX:, scaleY:, translateX:, translateY:, blur:, rotate:, originX:, originY:). At least one field. Used on Motion.pose.

constructors.name: Stagger
constructors.meaning: Stagger(step: Duration [, from: .first|.last]). Used on Motion.stagger. from defaults to .first.

constructors.name: Key
constructors.meaning: Key(pose: Pose | .rest, at: 0…1 [, ease:]). A waypoint on Motion.keys. `ease:` is the curve from this stop to the next; omit it to use the Motion clock.

constructors.name: Motion
constructors.meaning: Motion(transition: Transition [, play:] [, pose: Pose] [, keys: [Key, …]] [, stagger: Stagger] [, repeat: n]) or Motion(token, field:). The type of animate =. A bare Transition is sugar for Motion(transition: …). Site default fills play when omitted.

constructors.name: Effect
constructors.meaning: Effect(.blurSelf | .blurBehind | .glass, radius: [, vibrancy:]). Frame property `effect`. `blur = n` is sugar for `.blurSelf`. `.glass` is reserved. Not a layer and not a child.

constructors.name: MediaLayer
constructors.meaning: Media fill in a background/foreground stack: MediaLayer(source:, contentMode: … [, opacity:]). Produces token type Media. Do not postfix @ if opacity: is already set (PDL-E020).

constructors.name: IconRef
constructors.meaning: Concrete glyph: `IconRef(system: IconSystem, name: "…")` or `IconRef(file: "icons/…")`. This is the Icon token RHS — not the `Icon()` frame.

constructors.name: MediaSource
constructors.meaning: MediaSource(file: "…" [, kind:] [, format:]) or MediaSource(url: "…" [, kind:] [, format:]). Pack paths have no leading /.

declarations.name: import
declarations.meaning: Pull another file into this design. Paths are relative to the importing file. There is no export — names are visible after merge. Later files win for themes and components; a second token of the same name is PDL-E003. Cycles are PDL-E002.

declarations.name: previewBackground
declarations.meaning: The preview canvas color. Use a Color token, not a layout property.

declarations.name: primitive
declarations.meaning: A raw palette value (`#3B82F6`, `12`). Components should use semantic names instead.

declarations.name: semantic
declarations.meaning: An intent name components should use (`color.surface`, `space.stack`). Points at a primitive or another semantic.

declarations.name: theme
declarations.meaning: A named remap of tokens a person flips — light, dark, reduced motion. Body lines assign existing token names. Themes do not inherit from each other. Not for platform icon sets; those are `catalog`. Studio lists themes in the theme picker. Bake `--theme` accepts only themes. See Theme.

declarations.name: catalog
declarations.meaning: A named remap the environment applies — SF Symbols vs Material icons. Same override shape as a theme. Apply with `use catalog Name` inside `mount` only. Studio must not list catalogs in the theme picker. Token stack is base, then user theme(s), then catalogs (catalog wins on shared keys). See Catalog.

declarations.name: host
declarations.meaning: An environment profile. Params are what `<Host>` components read. Optional `mount` maps a facts bag onto those params. Every host in the design must share the same param names and types. See Host environment.

declarations.name: typeStyle
declarations.meaning: A named bundle of text-frame properties. A text frame sets `style = Title`. See typeStyle.

declarations.name: variant
declarations.form: variant Name { case a; case b }
declarations.meaning: A closed set of visual choices (tone, size). Write `.primary` at use sites. Same as enum in v1.

declarations.name: enum
declarations.form: enum Name { case a; case b }
declarations.meaning: Same as variant in v1. Prefer `enum` for ids (`FilterId`); prefer `variant` for visual axes.

declarations.name: protocol
declarations.form: protocol P: component { … }  or  protocol P { host … }
declarations.meaning: A shared contract. Use an API protocol so mixed chips share `select`; use a host protocol so the preview can deliver clicks.

declarations.name: component
declarations.meaning: A reusable UI piece: a name, public parameters, and one root frame.

declarations.name: page
declarations.meaning: A navigable destination. Same body machine as component. Auto-satisfies prelude `Page`, so a screen can take `content: Page = Home()`.

declarations.name: screen
declarations.meaning: A device shell. Same body machine as component. Studio lists screens as prototype roots. Mount `Presenter(root:)` next to chrome.

declarations.name: emits
declarations.form:
emits

or emits Name { channel(field: Type) } or emits(propagation: .ancestors) { … }
declarations.meaning:
`emits

` sends a named protocol (channels, params, `[P]` slots). `emits { … }` declares one-off channels. Default `.parent` stays at the declaring parent. `.ancestors` climbs until a sink that both lists `

` and writes `channel(…) =` stops it. Not a click from the preview — that is a host event.

declarations.name: fixtures
declarations.meaning: Named preview scenarios (“Empty search”, “Focus mood”). A bag of parameters — not data you put on screen. A Presenter let may be pinned as a stack (`presenter = [Home(), Episode()]`) and an optional cover (`presenter.cover = Settings()`).

declarations.name: samples
declarations.meaning: A reusable catalog of instances you mount so a prototype can stay interactive. Point at `Tracks.library.tracks`.

declarations.name: usage
declarations.meaning: A written note for authors and tools. In v1 the only key is `description`. See Usage.

declarations.name: rules
declarations.meaning: Checks the design can fail in preview or CI. Tags and Rule lines live only here. See Rule.

declarations.name: extend
declarations.meaning: Add fixtures, usage, or rules to an imported component without copying its layout. See Extend.

theme.meaning: A named override bundle. Each line is `tokenName = value`. The left side is a declared `primitive` or `semantic` (prefer semantics so components stay stable). The right side is a value of that token’s type — another token, or a literal. The assignment replaces the whole token; there is no field-by-field merge inside a Shadow or Transition. Themes do not inherit. Write one theme per concern (Dark, ReducedMotion) and combine them when you bake or in the Playground — not with `theme Child: Parent`.

accept.meaning: Declare a named bundle. Name is an identifier, not a string.
Remap a semantic to another token. Preferred.
Literal of the token’s type. Fine for a skin; prefer a token ref when the value is reused.
Replace a structured token wholly (Transition, Shadow, Background, …).

reject.meaning: Do not author parent/child themes. The `:` form is parsed but is not how themes combine.
No dotted field patch. Assign a new Shadow(…) to `shadow.card`.

theme.example:
primitive color.white: Color = #FFFFFF
primitive color.ink: Color = #111827
semantic color.surface: Color = color.white
semantic color.text: Color = color.ink

theme Dark {
  color.surface = color.ink
  color.text = color.white
}

catalog.meaning: A host-applied token remap. Write the same `token = value` lines as a theme. Do not put catalogs in the theme picker or pass them to bake `--theme` (PDL-E049). Apply them only with `use catalog Name` inside `mount`, so a platform tag can choose Apple icons vs Material icons. After user themes, a catalog wins on shared keys.

accept.meaning: Declare a named host remap. The name must not collide with a theme (PDL-E003).
Inside `mount` only. Applies immediately so later `if` arms see the new tokens.

reject.meaning: `Dark` is a theme. Catalogs and themes are different roles (PDL-E049).

reject.form: component C() layout { use catalog AppleIcons }
reject.meaning: `use catalog` outside `mount` is PDL-E047.

host.meaning: A `host` profile is the pack’s environment contract: named params with defaults, plus an optional `mount` that reads an opaque facts bag and writes those params. Components opt in with `<Host>` (prelude `protocol Host { host }` — no inbound channels). Bake picks a profile (requested name, else `Default`, else the sole host), starts at defaults, runs `mount` once, then any fact whose key equals a host param name pins that param. Every `<Host>` component in that bake sees the same bag. Author-declared params of the same name still win. `WindowSize` / `AppSurface` in labs are pack variants, not language types. Recommended fact keys (not required): `view.width`, `view.height`, `studio.platform`. Playground chrome and fixture `hostFacts` may send those keys, or pin `sizeClass` / `surface` directly.

accept.meaning: Profile + defaults + `mount`. Name one `Default` when several profiles exist.
Soft probe. A miss is none; `??` takes the next arm. Only inside `mount`.
Write the host param bag. `<Host>` injection reads this after `mount`.
Opt in. `if sizeClass == .compact` is legal. Without `<Host>` that read is PDL-E007.
A fact key that matches a host param pins the bag after `mount`. Playground WindowSize / AppSurface chrome uses this.

reject.form: host Phone(width: Distance = 390)  +  host Tablet(sizeClass: WindowSize = .medium)
reject.meaning: Every host in the design must share param names and types (PDL-E045). Defaults may differ.
Not in a component body or token RHS (PDL-E047).
Molecules do not read the environment. Put `<Host>` on a structural parent.

lets.meaning: A `let` names something inside a component. Prefer a lowercase id so it does not look like the type: `let title = Text(…)` is a nested frame you mount in `children`. `let save = Button(label: "Save")` is a component you declared — instantiate it in a layout the same way. `let ramp: Ramp = Ramp(…)` is a typed value you reuse in props or layers — it is not a view and must not appear in `children`. The id must be unique in the component. Write the `let` before any `children = [id]` or `id.prop` that names it (PDL-E019). A frame let mounts at most once (PDL-E042).

accept.meaning: Nested text frame. Mount with `children = [title]`.
Nested layout. Frame constructors: Layout, Text, Icon, Media, Presenter.

Navigation hole. `root` is required and must be a `page`. The hole accepts layout box props (`width`, `height`, `padding`, `align`, `justify`); `width` / `height` default to `.fill`. Command it from a capture: `presenter.push(Episode(id: id))` / `presenter.pop()` / `presenter.replace(…)` / `presenter.present(Settings(), style: .cover)` / `presenter.dismiss()`. Fixture pin: `presenter = [Home(), Episode()]` and `presenter.cover = Settings()`.
A component you declared. Pass its parameters; mount it in `children` like a frame.
Typed value. Reuse in `background = [ramp]`. Not mountable.
Assign after the let. The let must appear earlier in the body.

reject.meaning: Classic kind-colon form is removed (PDL-E001). Use `let id = Text(…)`.
A typed value let is not a frame. Put it on a property, not in children.
A let mounts once (PDL-E042). Write `let a = Button(); let b = Button()` or a list.

parameters.meaning: Every name in `component Name(…)` is public inbound surface. Write `name: Type = default`. Types are String, Number, Bool, a token type, a variant/enum you declared, a component or protocol name, or `[Type]` for a list of instances. There is no private parameter and no `expose` filter.

accept.meaning: Quoted string default.
Boolean. Write `Bool`, not `Boolean`.
Invert a Bool parameter in a host handler (or any Bool value position).
A variant/enum you declared. Default is a `.case`.
Token or value builtin, with a literal or token default.
Single slot — a component or protocol instance.
List of instances. Empty `[]` is allowed.

reject.meaning: `Boolean` is PDL-E039. Write `Bool`.

conditionals.meaning: An `if` / `else if` / `else` chain overrides properties when a parameter or state matches. The resolver walks top to bottom and applies only the first matching branch — there is no fall-through. A branch is a flat list of assignments, not a script. Bare `prop = value` updates the enclosing frame (usually the root). `id.prop = value` updates a let. Write the let before any `id.prop` or `children = [id]` (PDL-E019).

accept.meaning: First-match branch. Typical condition is `param == .case`.
Tried only when earlier branches missed.
No condition. Runs when nothing above matched. Omit it when the frame defaults already express the base state.
Dotted assign on a let. Prefer this over nesting `if` inside a constructor.
A Bool parameter is truthy as a condition.

reject.meaning: Two separate `if`s both run when they match. A chain is first-match only; later `else if` arms do not also apply.
Forward reference. The let must appear first (PDL-E019).

typeStyle.meaning: A named bundle of text-frame properties. Each line is `name = value` using the same property names as a text frame (`fontFamily`, `fontSize`, `fontWeight`, `lineHeight`, `letterSpacing`, …). A text frame applies the bundle with `style = Name`. Later frame props win over the style. `style = null` clears the binding.

accept.meaning: Declare a named bundle. Body is text-frame props only.
Apply the bundle on a text frame (constructor arg or assignment).
Clear the type-style binding without inventing typography literals.

reject.meaning: Layout props are not text-frame props.

null.meaning: The word `null` means pretend this property was never set. Use it on a frame or typeStyle property to erase a prior value so the default applies. It is not a Color, Opacity, or other token. `gap = null` clears `gap` only — it does not clear `columnGap` or `rowGap`.

accept.meaning: Unset. Often means absent (no border color).
Clear the type-style binding on a text frame.
After `style = Title`, clears that property even if the style contributed it.
Unsets `gap` only. Does not clear `columnGap` / `rowGap`.

reject.meaning: Not a token RHS (PDL-E005). Use a domain empty such as `borderWidth = 0` when that is the value.

conditions.meaning: What you write after `if` (and inside ForEach). Compare a parameter to a `.case`, test a Bool, negate, or combine with `&&` / `||`. Do not mix `&&` and `||` in one expression without parentheses.

accept.meaning: Parameter equals a variant case.
Same-type compare. `self.` is the enclosing component; bare `filter` is often a ForEach item field.
A Bool is truthy on its own.
Negation in a condition (`if !selected { … }`). Same `!` also inverts a Bool value (`isOn = !isOn`, `hidden = !selected`, kwargs).
Both. Do not mix with `||` unless you parenthesize.
Either. Do not mix with `&&` unless you parenthesize.

reject.meaning: Ambiguous. Write `(a && b) || c` or `a && (b || c)`.

syntax.meaning: Identifiers are letters, digits, `_`, and `.` where the grammar allows (`MyComponent`, `color.text.primary`). Line comments are `// …`. Block comments are `/* … */`. Hex colors are not strings — write `#RRGGBB`, not `"#RRGGBB"`. Numbers are unitless; there is no `px` suffix.

accept.meaning: To end of line. Treated as whitespace.
May span lines.
A Color literal, not a string.
Unitless number. Distance and Size are design units (pixels in HTML preview).

reject.meaning: Quoted hex is PDL-E017.
No unit suffix.

files.meaning: The entry `.pdl` file is the root of the merged design. `import "relative/path.pdl"` pulls another module. There is no export — after merge, names are just names. Paths are relative to the importing file. Token names (`primitive` / `semantic`) are unique across the graph (PDL-E003). Themes, components, and most other top-level kinds: later wins. Import cycles are PDL-E002. The entry file’s own declarations merge last.

accept.meaning: Relative to this file. Merges that module into the design.
Canvas color for preview. A Color token, not a layout property.

reject.meaning: There is no export keyword. Import the file that declares the name.
Cycles are PDL-E002.

reject.form: primitive color.ink: Color = #111 in two files
reject.meaning: Token redeclaration is PDL-E003.

arrayChildren.meaning: A list parameter (`chips: [FilterChip]`) mounts when it appears in `children`. `children = chips` and `children = [chips]` both splice the list in place. Mix siblings with brackets: `children = [header, chips, footer]`. A single slot (`content: ModalContent = UpsellBody()`) also expands in `children`. Dotted override `slot.field = value` is legal on a single slot — if `field` is a param it overrides the instance; otherwise it sets a root-frame prop. Array slots cannot use `slots.foo =` (PDL-E034); use ForEach.

accept.meaning: Mount the list. Same as `children = [chips]`.
Compose: lists splice among siblings.

reject.meaning: Dotted override on an array slot is PDL-E034. Use ForEach.

variants.meaning: A `variant` (and `enum`, the same construct in v1) is a finite set of named cases. Use it as a parameter type and in conditions. Case names are identifiers without dots. At use sites write `.caseName`. Prefer `variant` for visual axes (tone, size); prefer `enum` for ids and state sets. Tooling may treat the keywords differently later.

accept.form: variant BannerTone { case success; case warning }
accept.meaning: Declare cases. Semicolons or newlines are fine.

accept.form: enum FilterId { case all; case pop }
accept.meaning: Same as variant in v1.
Parameter type and `.case` default.
Compare to a case in a condition.

reject.meaning: Cases need the leading dot: `.success`.

self.meaning: `self` is the enclosing component instance — not a frame id. `self.param` in a value or condition names that component’s parameter (the escape hatch when a ForEach item field would shadow). `self.prop = value` (not a brace block) sets a root-frame property. `self.channel = { … }` is a host inbound handler (`self.` is optional in the kind body). Inside `rules`, `self` is the instance whose rules block is running — a different namespace.

accept.meaning: Enclosing component parameter. Prefer this in ForEach when the item might shadow the name.
Root frame property of this component — never an intermediate let.
Host inbound handler. Bare `pressEnd = { … }` is the same. Legal at the top of the kind body or inside layout `if` / `else` (conditions are preserved on the handler).
Rules-query `self` — the instance being checked, not layout `self`.

reject.meaning: `self` is not a frame id. Mount lets and slots, not `self`.

motion.meaning: Host handler bodies have one motion assignment: `animate =`. Its type is Motion — a Transition plus optional play, Pose or keys, Stagger, and finite repeat. A Transition token or tuple is sugar for `Motion(transition: …)`. `Motion(token, field:)` copies a Motion token and overrides labeled fields. Bake is the rest pose. The HTML host plays a CSS overlay — not layout. Units: Duration is milliseconds; translate and blur are CSS pixels; scale is unitless; opacity is 0…1; rotate is degrees; originX / originY are 0…1. Pose fields: `opacity`, `scale`, `scaleX`, `scaleY`, `translateX`, `translateY`, `blur`, `rotate`, `originX`, `originY`. Appear defaults to play toward rest; dismiss toward the last key; hoverStart / pressStart with a pose track default `.toPose`; hoverEnd / pressEnd default `.toRest`. Reusable tokens omit `play`. Pose / keys are legal on pointer handlers (flourish). `stagger` without a pose track is rejected.

accept.meaning: Transition sugar. Use this curve for property changes this handler triggers (implicit interpolation).

accept.form: animate = Motion(transition: motion.appear, pose: Pose(opacity: 0, scale: 0.95, translateY: 8))
accept.meaning: Lifecycle overlay. appear = from pose; dismiss = to pose.

accept.form: animate = Motion(transition: motion.appear, pose: pose.fadeUp, stagger: Stagger(step: 30, from: .first))
accept.meaning: Pose each direct visible child with this Transition; stagger them like this.
Copy a Motion token and override play (or any other field).
Standing overlay on a frame. Bake carries the Motion while the if is true; omit the field when false.
Same property on the component root.

reject.meaning: The `interaction` keyword is removed (PDL-E001). Put motion on `self.appear = { … }`.
Removed. Write `pose: Pose(opacity: 0)` on Motion.
Removed. Write `stagger: Stagger(step: 30, from: .first)` on Motion.
Stagger without pose is rejected.
Copy base must be a Motion token (PDL-E005).

eventDirections.name: emits
eventDirections.wire: `emit select(filter)` in a host handler; parent writes `item.select(…) = { … }`
eventDirections.meaning: The child tells the parent something happened (selected, changed).

eventDirections.name: host inbound
eventDirections.wire: `self.pressEnd = { … }` in the component body (self. is optional)
eventDirections.meaning: The preview tells the component the user hovered, clicked, or typed. Opt in with `<PointerInput>` or `<EditableText>`.

eventDirections.name: host verbs
eventDirections.meaning: The component asks the preview to do something — start or end typing.

emitForms.meaning: Declare what this component can tell its parent, in a separate block. Each field needs a type.
The same channels, written right after the component body.

This component sends that protocol — it may `emit` those channels, inherits the protocol’s params, and may fill a `[ShowEpisode]` / `[SubnavItem]` slot. Header form sits before `(params)`; trailing form sits after `}`.

emitForms.form: protocol P: component { emits { select(filter: FilterId) } }
emitForms.meaning: One shared channel for every component that follows the protocol — a mixed list of chips all `select`.
Same as omitting the argument. The immediate parent must capture on the child let.
Unhandled emits climb ancestors until a bare `showEpisode(id:) = { … }` stops them. Catalogue records `propagation` only when it is not `.parent`.
Ancestor capture on this node — usually the screen. The sink must also list the protocol in receive `<>` (`screen Phone <ShowEpisode>`). Not `ShowEpisode.showEpisode` and not `presenter.showEpisode`.
Fire the channel from a click (or other host handler). Pass values that match the declared types.
Send this whole instance to the parent — “open this row.”
The parent hears one named child (`All`) and updates its own state.
The parent hears each item in a list. Write this on `chip`, not on `chips`.

protocolForms.meaning: A contract for components that share parameters and emits. Use for mixed lists and slots.
A contract with the preview — clicks, editing. Not something you put in a list.
Receive list. Host inbound (`PointerInput`, `EditableText`, `Host`) and ancestor-sink APIs (`ShowEpisode`). Multiple sinks are allowed (`<ShowEpisode, AppNav>`).
Receive host clicks; send the nav protocol. Same protocol cannot appear in both lists.
Send / slot membership. Inherits `SubnavItem` params and `select`; `requires PointerInput` still applies. Param-only APIs (`ModalContent`, `Page`) use this form too.
The screen is the ancestor sink. It opts in with `<>` and writes the bare handler. Emitters write `emits <ShowEpisode>`.
Read the active `host` profile’s params. No clicks or typing — that is PointerInput / EditableText. See Host environment.
A destination. Auto-satisfies prelude `Page` without writing `<Page>`.

protocolForms.form: screen Phone() layout { let presenter = Presenter(root: home) … }
protocolForms.meaning: A shell. Mount a `Presenter` next to chrome. `Page` is a prelude API protocol; only `page` declarations (or `component C emits <Page>`) fill `root`.
This API protocol also needs preview events (clicks or typing).
A parameter every conforming component has.

hostProtocols.name: PointerInput
hostProtocols.meaning: Use this when a component should react to hover, click, focus, or appear/dismiss — a button that changes color on hover, a chip that selects on click. Write `component Chip <PointerInput>` then `self.pressEnd = { … }`.

inbound.name: pressEnd
inbound.meaning: Pointer or button went up — the usual tap / click complete.

inbound.name: pressCancel
inbound.meaning: The press was aborted (drag-off or system cancel).

inbound.name: activate
inbound.meaning: Primary activation (Enter / accessibility activate), distinct from press.

inbound.name: appear
inbound.meaning: The component became visible / entered the tree.

inbound.name: dismiss
inbound.meaning: The host asked this component to dismiss (sheet, modal).

hostProtocols.name: EditableText
hostProtocols.meaning: Use this for a field the user can type into. Pair with kind `text`. The preview starts editing on click or focus by default. Show the typed string with `content = self.value`.

inbound.name: editingCancelled
inbound.meaning: The session aborted. Restore the checkpoint.

verbs.name: beginEditing
verbs.meaning: Start a session seeded with this string.

verbs.name: cancelEditing
verbs.meaning: Abort the session and restore the checkpoint.

injected.name: value
injected.meaning: What the user has typed. Default "".

injected.name: isEditing
injected.meaning: True while the field is being edited.

injected.name: isOverLimit
injected.meaning: True when `value` is longer than the host limit.

hostProtocols.name: Host
hostProtocols.meaning: Opt in to read the active host profile’s params (`sizeClass`, `previewBackground`, or whatever the pack declared). No inbound channels and no verbs. Use on structural parents only: `component Shell <Host>()` or `component Shell <Host, PointerInput>()`. Bake injects one bag for the whole design: host defaults, then `mount` against `hostFactsJson`, then any fact whose key matches a host param (Playground WindowSize / AppSurface chrome, or a fixture pin). Author params of the same name still win. Reading a host param without `<Host>` is PDL-E007.

preludeEnums.name: TextFieldActivation
preludeEnums.meaning: When a text field starts editing. Use `.focus` for the usual click-or-focus field; `.none` if only your code should start editing.

cases.meaning: Default. Click, tap, or focus begins editing.
Begin on press/click only — not bare focus.
Program-only. Call beginEditing yourself; the leaf hit-test does not begin.

forEachForms.meaning: For each item in the list, write overrides and listen for clicks. The name `chip` is the current item.
Put the list on screen. ForEach does not do this by itself. Use brackets when mixing siblings: `[Header, chips, Footer]`.
Set each item from parent state — which chip looks selected. Use `self.` when the parent and item share a name.
Hear that item’s emit. Write `chip.select`, not `chips.select`.

forEachForms.form: if self.currentFilter == filter { chip.selected = true } else { … }
forEachForms.meaning: Same `if` / `else` as layout, evaluated per list item. Prefer `chip.selected = self.currentFilter == filter` when one Bool is enough.
Reserved list chrome. Compilers reject these (PDL-E026). Do not invent dividers this way.

repeatForms.meaning: Mount `numberOfPages` children. Binder `i` runs 1 … N by default.

repeatForms.form: let dots = Repeat(count: n) { i in … }; children = dots
repeatForms.meaning: Name a Repeat, then mount it like any other child. Same bake expansion as `children = Repeat(…)`.
Equality against another Number param — selection chrome without layout math.

sampleForms.meaning: Declare a named catalog. A later `samples Tracks` replaces the earlier one. The name must not collide with a component.
One named slice of the catalog (`focus`, `empty`). Fields are typed. An empty list is real data — no rows.
Point at one field: bank, then entry, then field. Use in defaults or layout so the prototype can switch data.

fixtures.meaning: Write `fixtures Component { … }` next to the component (or inside `extend`). Each `example "Label" { … }` is one row in the Fixture menu. The body assigns that component’s parameters to concrete values — a string, a `.case`, a sample path. It may also pin bake knobs: `host`, `theme`, and `hostFacts` (a JSON object string). Those are not component params. It does not write layout, and it does not read other parameters.

accept.meaning: Named scenarios for one component. The quoted label is what you pick in the Fixture menu.
One scenario. Every assignment is a concrete value.
Pin the host profile and facts bag so review SoT does not depend on Playground resize. A fact key that matches a host param (`sizeClass`, `surface`) pins that param after `mount`.
A field may point at a sample. The fixture still chooses the world; the sample is the catalog.

reject.meaning: Not another parameter. Write a literal or a sample path.
`usage`, `rules`, and `extend` are their own blocks. A fixtures block is only examples.

usage.meaning: A written note attached to a component. Authors and tools read it; it does not change layout. In v1 the only key is `description`. Write `usage Button { … }` next to the component (or inside `extend`).

accept.meaning: Replace the note. The name is the component, not a string.
Append with a single space. Use this inside `extend` so a project can add a sentence without wiping the imported note.

reject.meaning: Unknown keys are not defined in v1. Only `description`.
`usage` is a top-level companion, not a frame property.

extend.meaning: Add fixtures, usage, or rules to a component that already exists — usually one you imported — without copying its layout. Inner sections follow the same rules as standalone blocks. `description =` replaces; `description +=` appends. A later `tags =` replaces the whole tags array; `Rule(…)` lines append.

accept.meaning: Add or replace a fixture by its label.
Append to the imported note.
Append a check. `tags =` in a later file replaces the tags array.

reject.meaning: Only components. There is no `extend` for a variant or token.
Extend does not edit layout. Change the source component, or wrap it.

rule.meaning: Write `Rule(strength, query)` inside `rules Component { … }`. The query is true or false from this instance. `.must` / `.mustNot` fail validation; `.should` / `.shouldNot` warn. Optional `description:` is what authors see. `tags =` replaces the tag list; `tags.add` appends. An `if` in this block chooses tags and Rule lines from parameters — it does not restyle the frame. Rules-query `self` is this instance, not layout `self`.

accept.meaning: Attach checks to a component. Tags are strings this instance can be found by.
If the query matches, fail. Optional `description` is what authors see.
A softer check. Rules-query `self` is this instance — not layout `self`.
Inside `rules`, `if` chooses tags and Rule lines from parameters. It does not restyle the frame.
Order in the parent’s children. Also `.follows` and `.adjacentTo`.

reject.meaning: Tags are not frame properties. Put them in `rules`.
`Rule` is not a frame constructor. It only belongs in `rules`.

examples.title: One primary action
How many tabs
Sit last in the parent
A label before the field
Do not leave a card empty

ruleQuery.meaning: Use rules to catch design mistakes the preview or CI can flag — only one primary button, a tab bar must have 2–5 tabs. An `if` in a frame changes how something looks; a Rule does not.

navigators.name: self
navigators.meaning: This component instance (the one whose `rules` block is running).

navigators.name: parent
navigators.meaning: The instance that contains this one. Empty at the design root.

navigators.name: siblings
navigators.meaning: Other children of the same parent.

filters.meaning: Keep instances tagged with that name. Tags come only from `rules` blocks.

ordering.meaning: Some match appears before self in the parent’s children order.
Some match is immediately next to self.
